protections: execute_sql read-only gate: the request is split with splitSQLStatements and every statement's first keyword must be in the per-dialect allow-list after comments/strings are stripped (src/tools/execute-sql.ts:26-29,58-63; src/utils/allowed-keywords.ts:75-123).

Custom-tool read-only gate: the same classifier is applied to the whole operator-configured statement, without splitting (src/tools/custom-tool-handler.ts:186 via src/utils/tool-handler-helpers.ts:36).
Per-execution engine enforcement keyed on ExecuteOptions.readonly, declared in the connector contract but implemented by no connector (src/connectors/interface.ts:62-71).

Connection-level read-only keyed on ConnectorConfig.readonly, implemented only for PostgreSQL (default_transaction_read_only) and SQLite (readOnly open), and unreachable from TOML (src/connectors/postgres/index.ts:175-178; src/connectors/sqlite/index.ts:184-194; src/config/toml-loader.ts:628-634).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: src/connectors/interface.ts:66-70 defines ExecuteOptions.readonly as application-level keyword validation already performed at the tool gate, and docs/tools/execute-sql.mdx:129 calls read-only mode a safety net rather than a security boundary, so the connector reads as the wrong layer.
The mariadb connector is a line-for-line mirror of the mysql one and both are registered implementations of the same interface, so a fix made in src/connectors/mysql/index.ts is assumed to cover it.
MySQL is the dialect the tool gate already splits and classifies statement by statement, and the pooled connection is borrowed and released per call, so a guard inside executeSQL looks redundant.

SQLite keeps one process-local handle opened at connect and a :memory: database cannot be opened read-only (src/connectors/sqlite/index.ts:185,192), so read-only can only be a keyword decision made above the connector.

T-SQL has no READ ONLY transaction, mssql is an optional driver, the published fix is scoped to the four dialects it patched, and the product docs call read-only mode a safety net rather than a security boundary (docs/tools/execute-sql.mdx:129).

pragma is SQLite's introspection keyword and the pinned unit test requires PRAGMA table_info(users) to be read-only (src/utils/__tests__/allowed-keywords.test.ts:62-63), so rejecting pragmas or their parenthesised/equals forms would break legitimate schema discovery.
A source configured for read-only is read-only for every tool on it, so switching the connection or session at connect time is simpler and is assumed to cover every call.

The statement is operator-authored TOML, the parameters are bound (src/tools/custom-tool-handler.ts:193-203), and docs/tools/custom-tools.mdx:233-252 say custom tools are not affected by execute_sql's readonly setting, so the route is not attacker-controlled.
Two dashes begin a comment in SQL, so the whitespace/control-character nuance of MySQL and MariaDB reads as an obscure lexical detail that the connector-level backstop will cover anyway.

Connection-level read-only already exists for PostgreSQL (src/connectors/postgres/index.ts:175-178) and SQLite (src/connectors/sqlite/index.ts:184-194), so the lower layer looks partly covered and the per-tool check above it looks sufficient.
The statement starts with SELECT, the documented read-only keyword, and what a called function does to the database is the database's business, not the classifier's.

masking: Once a connector rejects the write at execution time, a hidden test that only asserts the write failed passes while the classifier still accepts SQLite PRAGMA setters (T6) and the MySQL/MariaDB dash-dash form (T9), so the tool gate's own contract (READONLY_VIOLATION) is no longer observed.

The connect-time producer path (T10) is dead config: src/config/toml-loader.ts:628-634 rejects a source-level readonly and src/types/config.ts:49-59 has no field, so once per-execution enforcement works no test observes that the connection-level path never fires.

conflicts.what: The simplest backstop for T1 (connection- or session-wide read-only: default_transaction_read_only, a session read-only flag, node:sqlite readOnly, PRAGMA query_only left on) breaks a writable tool on the same source, because there is one connector instance per source (src/connectors/manager.ts:231,262) and pooled connections are reused (src/connectors/mysql/index.ts:613,660) — exactly the coupled value T7 protects.

Closing the PRAGMA setter hole by rejecting every pragma that carries an equals sign or parentheses also rejects PRAGMA table_info(users), which the pinned unit test (src/utils/__tests__/allowed-keywords.test.ts:62-63) and the SQLite connector's read classification (src/connectors/sqlite/index.ts:464-472) require.

fairness_risks: PRAGMA table_info(users) must stay read-only-allowed (src/utils/__tests__/allowed-keywords.test.ts:62-63) while PRAGMA setters are the hole in T6; a reject-all-pragma rule contradicts a pinned test.

EXPLAIN DELETE FROM users must stay allowed (src/utils/__tests__/allowed-keywords.test.ts:171-173) while EXPLAIN ANALYZE with DML must be rejected (src/utils/__tests__/allowed-keywords.test.ts:176-198); a rule that descends into the statement under EXPLAIN breaks the first.
SELECT REPLACE(name,'a','b') must stay allowed (src/utils/__tests__/allowed-keywords.test.ts:75-82); a blanket rejection of the replace token breaks it.

Tools with readonly false or undefined on the same source must keep writing (src/tools/__tests__/execute-sql.test.ts:215-233), so enforcement has to be per call and a connection-level switch is refused.
A :memory: SQLite source cannot be opened read-only (src/connectors/sqlite/index.ts:185,192); an open-read-only rule breaks in-memory databases.

MySQL/MariaDB executable comments /*! ... */ and /*M! ... */ must stay executable text (src/utils/__tests__/sql-parser.test.ts:49-73); a strip-all-comments simplification contradicts existing pinned behaviour.

The custom-tool statement is operator-authored TOML with bound parameters (src/tools/custom-tool-handler.ts:193-203), so a rule that splits it at semicolons refuses a shape only an operator can produce — low security value, real fairness cost.

design.why: Five independent fix sites across four layers, each with a different reason to leave it alone: the Postgres connector never consumes ExecuteOptions.readonly on either the single-statement or the batch path (M4, dismissal: the interface says this is application-level work already done above); MariaDB is a separately written connector that a MySQL fix does not reach (M2, dismissal: it mirrors MySQL); the SQLite connector has the same missing enforcement behind a shared in-process handle (M4, dismissal: :memory: cannot be opened read-only); the SQLite PRAGMA allow-list entry makes every pragma form read-only, coupled to the pinned PRAGMA table_info test (M11, MiMo-style over-hardening); and the two-dash comment scanner mis-splits exactly the MySQL/MariaDB form the engine executes (M8, how-type). It beats the alternatives because it needs no SQL Server instance, every trap is exercised by a site the published fix itself touches, and the two must-keep-working values (PRAGMA table_info, writable tools on the same source) make the naive over-broad fixes fail visibly. T5 (SQL Server, absent backstop plus the strongest dismissal) is the best extra reasoning trap but needs an injected sqlserver test and a well-specified T-SQL guard, so it is the first add-on rather than part of the core; T8 (custom tool) is excluded because its input is operator-authored; T10 and T11 are sub-decisions inside the T1 group (wrong layer and first-keyword-only shapes).

unverified: The published fix commit 872bb338f7d31f6afe517a076ac3e3edafaaaf08 was not readable in this worktree (HEAD is the pinned commit), so the claim that the fix adds a per-execution engine backstop in four connectors comes from the screener record, not from code.
Whether a READ ONLY transaction permits EXPLAIN of a DML statement on PostgreSQL or MySQL was reasoned from documentation only; no database was run.

SQL Server reachability of a write through the keyword gate was reasoned from code only; no SQL Server instance was run, and the connector's EXPLAIN path (src/connectors/sqlserver/index.ts:711-754) was not executed.
The exact number of distinct fix hunks (16 per the candidate metadata) was not reconciled site-by-site; the sites recorded here are the ones groundable in the pinned tree.
Repository size was not measured in this environment.
